post_src_ign_0772d77cce8f8c94.title: Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 — Everything Announced
post_src_ign_0772d77cce8f8c94.description: Microsoft hit Tokyo Game Show 2026 with a special Xbox broadcast event, and IGN has a roundup of everything announced.
post_src_ign_0772d77cce8f8c94.content:
Microsoft's Tokyo Game Show 2026 Xbox broadcast is over, and we've got everything announced right here so you can catch up with all the news.
We got the campaign trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and confirmation that Mads Mikkelsen is in the game. We also got new trailers for Sega's Crazy Taxi World Tour, ArtPlay's Bloodstained: The Scarlet Engagement, and Atlus' Persona 4 Revival. I thought Raji: Kaliyuga looked pretty cool, too.
But the headline news here came from Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima, who provided development updates on OD and Physint, now both Xbox games. We have confirmation of the actor playing the lead role in Physint, and a cool first-look poster. Neither game has a release date yet. 
If you need a catch-up, everything announced is below. And let us know what you're looking forward to in the comments!
And that's a wrap!Microsoft's TGS broadcast is over, and there was plenty in there for fans to get excited about. Let us know what you thought of the show in the comments.
Hideo Kojima!Hideo Kojima did indeed turn up at the end of the Xbox broadcast to talk about Kojima Productions' partnership with Microsoft. He spoke about meeting new Xbox boss Asha Sharma to discuss the future of video games. As we know, Kojima is working on OD – KNOCK for Xbox, with production "proceeding on schedule." Expect more information "later down the line."
And Kojima mentioned Physint as a new Xbox game. He says it's the "culimation of more than 40 years of my career." It's making "steady progress," he added. Kojima also revealed the actor for the lead role... Bill Skarsgård! Expect more casting announcements in the future. "This has been Hideo Kojima," he signed off.
Well, that was a surprise!
Bloodstained: The Scarlet EngagementWe got a fresh look at side-scrolling action game Bloodstained: The Scarlet Engagement during the show. ArtPlay revealed new gameplay from Koji Igarashi's new metroidvania, set in the gothic world of 16th Century England. The new trailer showcases the game’s fast-paced 2.5D action, with protagonists Leo and Alex battling their way through formidable enemies while exploring a sprawling, cursed land. Expect a release date in 2027.
Genigods: NezhaWe got a detailed look at Genigods: Nezha, an action RPG rooted in ancient Chinese genesis mythology from Genigods Lab, coming out in 2028. Here's the official blurb:
Genigods: Nezha is an ARPG rooted in the chaos of ancient Chinese creation mythology. Play as Spirit Pearl, the first being forged by the Goddess of Creation Nüwa. Dive into iconic Chinese genesis tales, battle Colossal Gods, and experience the unique combat of Chinese-style celestial showdowns.Edge of MemoriesMidgar Studios' Edge of Memories got a new trailer. This is another French studio's take on the JRPG genre, and it's due out November 5, 2026.
Developed through a collaboration between a small French studio and veteran Japanese developers, this gorgeous anime-style world is threatened by a mysterious disease that corrupts the land as you progress through the story, opening new paths in areas you’ve already explored.Join Eline and her companions on a journey to stop the spread of the Corrosion and save their home. The latest trailer showcases the Japanese dub, featuring a cast of renowned Japanese voice actors. Whether you’re playing in English or Japanese, pre-order Edge of Memories now on Xbox Series X and S.Once Human: Isles of AbyssOnce Human: Isles of Abyss got a release date reveal trailer. The free-to-play "strange worlds survival game" releases the Isles of Abyss expansion on October 22 on Xbox Series X and S with full cross-play. Once Human is already available now with Xbox Game Pass.
Raji: KaliyugaI thought Raji: Kaliyuga was one of the standout games from Xbox's TGS broadcast. The developer commentary video, from Indian studio Nodding Heads Games, focused on gameplay and gave us a good look at what to expect from combat. Raji: Kaliyuga features dual protagonists: Raji, with acrobatic martial arts and the Trishul, and Darsh, with immense Siddhi powers that control gravity, time, and energy. It introduces customized evasion for Raji and a siddhi-yielding system for Darsh, allowing unique combat styles. The game shifts from an isometric action-adventure to a third-person action-adventure.
Raji: Kaliyuga is coming to Xbox Series X and S and Xbox on PC as an Xbox Play Anywhere title and with Xbox Game Pass. Certainly one to watch.
Atelier Karia: The Night Kingdom & the Guide of MemoriesKoei Tecmo showed a new trailer for Atelier Karia: The Night Kingdom & the Guide of Memories, due out in February. It confirms the return of Rutger and Lenja from Atelier Yumia. Now experienced members of the Aladiss Pioneering Team, the two support Karia and her companions on their new adventure, with their interactions with new companions revealing new sides of both returning characters.
Atelier Karia tells the story of Karia, who has no memories, as she faces her past. New features add to the strategy of battles and depth of alchemy. Synthesized items take on new roles during exploration, and ingredients can be eaten to gain effects.Faraday BluesWe got a world premiere! Serenity Forge, the publisher of Vivarium, revealed surreal sci-fi adventure Faraday Blues. The game is three interconnected visual novels about a daughter searching for parents who don’t know she exists. It's coming to Xbox Series X and S and PC in 2027, with Xbox Cloud support.
BloomwalkerStudio Ghibli-inspired cozy crafting adventure Bloomwalker is "joining the Ni no Kuni universe," Xbox has confirmed. Players travel with a moving house to cleanse the pollution spreading across the land, restoring its sanctuaries and freeing its guardians. It's coming to Xbox Series X and S and Xbox on PC.
Hope in the CityWe got an extended look at Lofty Sky's Hope in the City. Here's the official description:
17-year-old Hope Song thought the national exams were her biggest worry... until she got home to a ransacked apartment and two missing parents. Investigate through the eyes of an artist, turn sketches into evidence, and watch her family's mystery grow stranger and darker with every answer.Hope in the City is a narrative mystery game played through the eyes of an artist: investigate, turn sketches into evidence, and watch your family's mystery grow stranger and darker with every answer. Hope in the City comes to Xbox Series X and S, Xbox on PC, and Game Pass on November 10, 2026, with Xbox Play Anywhere support.
Wo Long 2: Wings of EmberWo Long 2: Wings of Ember turned up with a fresh look at combat and the reveal of a boss fight. A demo is out now. The full game is coming March 4, 2027, and will be on Game Pass.
Shape of DreamsShape of Dreams, a co-op action roguelite, is available today for Xbox Series X and S and is day one with Xbox Game Pass. The Xbox version launches alongside the game’s first anniversary update, The Starless Path, which adds a new Traveler, a new final boss, and a new ending.
Persona 4 RevivalPersona 4 Revival got a new trailer, showing off a brief look at Atlus' game. It's due out next year, and is coming to Game Pass.

The campaign video sets up iconic hero Captain Price as the target this time. A face-off with Ghost is inevitable. And we also have confirmation that Mads Mikkelsen is in the game!
Here's the official blurb from Xbox:
The official Campaign trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is now live. It digs deep into the story, centered on John Price's shadow operations, including conflict with former allies and alliances with a former foe. Experience the invasion of South Korea and the threat of a weapon that could overturn the world order in the hands of the villainous Archer.Crazy Taxi World TourSega showed off a look at Japan in Crazy Taxi World Tour, coming out next year. "Japan: A place beautifully suspended between two worlds," reads the official description. "Here, historic neighborhoods and tradition sit alongside the bustling energy of the modern city. Get ready to fall in love with the land of the rising sun when Crazy Taxi: World Tour hits the streets in 2027!"

"Explore the vibrant world of Gachiakuta, brought to life with premium cartoon-style rendering and evocative visual design."

post_src_ign_1c8ed99b8498f210.title: Twitch Boss Says Game Companies Are Right to Avoid Competing With GTA 6 for Attention — Expects GTA Online 2 Next Year
post_src_ign_1c8ed99b8498f210.description: Twitch boss Dan Clancy has said he expects an enormous launch for GTA 6 this November, one video game companies are right to avoid like the plague. But he also expects GTA 6 to continue to hoover up the internet’s attention when GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called —  launches next year.
post_src_ign_1c8ed99b8498f210.content:
Twitch boss Dan Clancy has said he expects an enormous launch for GTA 6 this November, one video game companies are right to avoid like the plague. But he also expects GTA 6 to continue to hoover up the internet’s attention when GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called —  launches next year.
Speaking to Bloomberg, Clancy said he’d spoken with Rockstar Games about what the developer has up its sleeve.
“We spent a lot of time talking with Rockstar about their plans, and also helping them think about how they can engage our creators,” Clancy said. “You are going to see this big bump with GTA 6, but then an even bigger one next year when they launch multiplayer.”
Rockstar is yet to say when the multiplayer portion of GTA 6 will come out, or even confirm it plans to release a GTA Online 2, even though everyone knows it’s in the works. There is intense speculation about when it will release, or, more specifically, how long Rockstar will wait to deploy it after GTA 6’s November release date. Early 2027? Mid 2027? Late 2027? Either way, next year looks nailed on.
Will GTA Online 2 make the existing GTA Online redundant? Not necessarily. Last year, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, said Take-Two has form when it came to NBA 2K Online, a free-to-play online-focused version of 2K Sports’ hugely successful basketball franchise aimed at the Asian market. NBA 2K Online launched all the way back in 2012, and then 2K Sports released NBA 2K Online 2 in 2017. Both games were maintained simultaneously, so fans of the first version could continue to play and invest their time and money safe in the knowledge they wouldn’t be left behind.
“I'm going to speak theoretically only because I'm not going to talk about a particular project when an announcement hasn't been made,” Zelnick told IGN. “But generally speaking, we support our properties when the consumers are involved with those titles. As an example, we launched NBA 2K Online in China, I think originally in 2012 if I'm not mistaken. And then we launched NBA 2K Online 2 in China in 2017. If I'm not mistaken. We did not sunset Online 1. They both are still in the market and they serve consumers and they're alive and we have this massive audience.
“So we've shown a willingness to support legacy titles when a community wants to be engaged with them.”
That last line is of particular importance. It suggests — but doesn’t confirm at this stage — that if there is a GTA Online 2, it won’t come at the cost of GTA Online falling by the wayside. If people keep playing GTA Online, Zelnick is suggesting here, then Rockstar will continue to support it. And let's remember, GTA 6 launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S only. PC players' only option is to join the console party, or stick with GTA 5 and GTA Online on PC.
With November fast approaching, Rockstar has begun to reveal more about GTA 6 and how it will play. Just this week a number of artists teased their appearance on the GTA 6 soundtrack, and Stephen Root, who voices Bill Dauterive and Buck Strickland on the animated series King of the Hill, confirmed his role in the GTA 6 cast.
Remarkably, Rockstar has yet to confirm any GTA 6 actors, leading fans to try to work out the cast for themselves. We don’t even know who plays Jason and Lucia, the game’s dual protagonists. Perhaps we won’t until the game is out in November and the credits roll.
While you wait to find out, check out IGN’s extensive GTA 6 coverage, including our interview with Rockstar’s Rob Nelson on what to expect.

post_src_ign_413f594e0ec07480.title: Lollipop Chainsaw 2 Back2Back Announced, With Juliet Starling Now on Skates
post_src_ign_413f594e0ec07480.description: Zombie killing cheerleader Juliet Starling will return in Lollipop Chainsaw 2 Back2Back, it was announced today.
post_src_ign_413f594e0ec07480.content:
Zombie killing cheerleader Juliet Starling will return in Lollipop Chainsaw 2 Back2Back, it was announced today.
Set to launch on PlayStation 5 at some point in 2027, this long-awaited sequel features more fast-paced undead slicing, and even more of its plucky heroine Juliet, who appears to be wearing an even shorter skirt.
The original Lollipop Chainsaw debuted in 2012, and found cult status. It featured a witty script, partly penned James Gunn (before his days making Marvel and DC movies), and was the overall brainchild of Suda51, the legendary Japanese creator behind No More Heroes, Shadows of the Damned and a slew of other offbeat ideas.
15 years on, however, neither Gunn or Suda51 are contributing to this sequel. Instead, it is the work of Dragami Games, which previously released a remaster of the original Lollipop Chainsaw to a mixed response. Today's footage has also sparked a range of reactions on social media, where many have suggested that this sequel looks unpolished.
Lollipop Chainsaw 2 Back2Back has been announced for PS5 and a gameplay video has been released!
It will launch in 2027 pic.twitter.com/qXiwOhRW6V
— Game Unlocked (@gameunlocked26) September 17, 2026 "Juliet returns, in a brand-new outfit and with even more power, to a rebuilt San Romero, now transformed into 'Jaredwood,' a sprawling metropolis built around the film industry," reads a blurb for the new game. When a mysterious director traps her inside his twisted zombie movie, Juliet must fight alongside her allies, uncover the conspiracy behind the chaos, and stop a new threat posed by the Corrupted Realm zombies."
Footage revealed today as part of Tokyo Games Show 2026 featured Juliet slicing up zombies on a street, where her new rollerskates allow her to zip about at a faster speed. Further footage revealed a boss battle against Zorbie, a zombie that appears to be a riff on Barbie.
Last year, a Lollipop Chainsaw anime series was also announced as being in development. There's no further word on that today.

post_src_ign_4d4c4251ec9382e4.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Expected to Break Franchise Box Office Record, Topping 2010's Resident Evil: Afterlife
post_src_ign_4d4c4251ec9382e4.description: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil is expected to make more money at the box office on opening weekend than any other Resident Evil movie before it.
post_src_ign_4d4c4251ec9382e4.content:
Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil is expected to make more money at the box office on opening weekend than any other Resident Evil movie before it.
Resident Evil: Afterlife currently holds the domestic opening weekend box office record for the franchise, with $26.6 million back in 2010 (not adjusted for inflation). Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil, according to Variety, is targeting $40-50 million, but some believe it could end up near $60 million.
Deadline reports Resident Evil is expected to add $31 million overseas for a global total of around $80 million. Given Sony reportedly spent $75 million producing the movie (not including marketing spend), $80 million would be a fantastic start. Cregger brings with him added interest due to his past work on breakout horror movies, including Weapons. Sony will be hoping for more of the same with Resident Evil.
Afterlife, by the way, ended up with $300 million globally from theaters, so Cregger and co certainly have their work cut out topping that. Resident Evil: The Final Chapter — the last of the Paul W. S. Anderson / Milla Jovovich Resident Evil movies — ended with $312 million globally in 2017. It is currently the highest grossing Resident Evil movie.
IGN’s Resident Evil review returned an 8/10. We said: “With a laser focus on putting its hero through the worst night of his life, Resident Evil is a simple and exciting survival horror story that benefits greatly from director Zach Cregger’s sensibilities.”
The movie’s apparent inevitable success comes despite deep-rooted skepticism from some Resident Evil fans who wanted a more faithful adaptation of the video games. Cregger himself has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating this skepticism, which began when it was confirmed that his adaptation wouldn’t feature any characters from the video games, or tell any of the stories already told in the video games. Instead, Cregger has charted his own path, telling a horror story set in the world of Resident Evil that references some of the video games' tropes.
Cregger recently told IGN’s Tom Jorgensen: “I think I was naive. I thought fans of these games, like me, would be thrilled that somebody was coming along and turning Resident Evil into a survival horror movie. I was like, ‘That’s great.’ I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing. I get it, I understand the frustration. I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?”
“My only hope is that they’ll see the movie regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment that I’m not telling some of the stories that the games tell so well, and they will feel seen when they do watch the movie, and they will recognize all of the love for the games that are in this movie, because it is there,” he continued.
“This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story. I understand the resistance, I do, because I have it myself. It is coming from a true place of love.”
Last week, Cregger revealed he cut most of the jokes in Resident Evil, after test audiences apparently found the film "too funny." Cregger has also revealed who he'd cast as Lady Dimitrescu if he ever got the chance.

post_src_ign_5be866dceb4cfe8a.title: Bungie Denies Rumor It Plans to Merge the Destiny and Marathon IPs, Confirms Marathon December and March 2027 Updates Are Free
post_src_ign_5be866dceb4cfe8a.description: Bungie has stepped in to deny a rumor that it planned to merge the Destiny and Marathon IPs amid continued questions about the future of both franchises.
post_src_ign_5be866dceb4cfe8a.content:
Bungie has stepped in to deny a rumor that it planned to merge the Destiny and Marathon IPs amid continued questions about the future of both franchises.
The rumor, which has been doing the rounds online this week, was that Bungie was testing reworking Marathon and Destiny into a single IP. But, according to Marathon creative director Julia Nardin, that’s untrue.
“As someone who’s worked on both Destiny and Marathon, I can confirm that the “leak” about us merging the two IPs is fake,” Nardin said in a post on Twitter / X. “They share a lot of the same Bungie DNA, but like siblings they’re also their own independent entities. Please don’t believe everything you read online.”
It has of course been a tumultuous time for Bungie, Destiny, and Marathon. Marathon began life as an ultra hardcore extraction shooter, but Bungie has been retooling it to play more like Destiny since as the game has struggled for players. Meanwhile, Bungie stopped work on Destiny 2 to focus on Marathon — upsetting Destiny fans in the process. Livestreams from Bungie parent company Sony Interactive Entertainment have been overrun by calls for Bungie to return to the world of Destiny, either to continue with Destiny 2 or work on Destiny 3.
This week, Bungie announced a move away from seasonal content, a focus on PvE, and a significant delay for Marathon’s next update. It was slated to release on September 22, but will now arrive on December 8. A further significant update will be released in March. On October 6, Marathon will get a smaller update that resets progression and the in-game economy to prepare for an overhaul.
In a social media follow-up, Bungie clarified that the December and March updates are free, not paid DLC. “If you own Marathon, the December and March updates will be available at no additional cost,” the studio said. “That includes gameplay content such as new zones, weapons, and Runners.”
Which begs the question: why issue this clarification? Some believe it suggests a move to free-to-play supported by paid expansions, and these updates should not be confused with expansion-type content. However, Bungie hasn't announced any expansions for Marathon. Perhaps the plan is for different editions of Marathon, some paid, that would sit alongside a free offering. These might offer different tiers of content, allowing players to pick and choose.
The spectre in all this is of course Sony’s ongoing commitment to Marathon. It backed the game publicly, but some fans are worried about its future. Steam concurrents do not paint the full picture of a multiplatform game, but it’s worth noting that Marathon had a 24-hour peak of 2,464 on Valve’s platform, down from an all-time peak of 77,358 set when the game launched in March.

post_src_ign_637aee04d3406ea3.title: Spotify Seems to Be Teasing a GTA 6 Collaboration with Rockstar Games
post_src_ign_637aee04d3406ea3.description: Spotify appears to be the next big streaming giant to partner with Rockstar Games for GTA 6's marketing.
post_src_ign_637aee04d3406ea3.content:
Spotify appears to be the next big streaming giant to partner with Rockstar Games for GTA 6's marketing.
The music streaming service has begun putting up billboards in Los Angeles and New York featuring the GTA 6 artwork that was released by various artists yesterday. Travis Scott, Future, Morgan Wallen, and a handful of other musicians all posted unique artwork that resembled Rockstar's signature style, but neglected to reveal exactly what they were teasing. This cryptic tease now appears to involve Spotify. 
Many assumed that this was Rockstar's way of teasing these artists might have music in the game, but it may be much bigger than that. Some running theories have speculated that the artists could release  exclusive music for GTA 6, something Rockstar did with Dr. Dre for a GTA Online update a few years ago. However, Spotify's inclusion may mean there's even more to this; the platform might provide exclusive teases of some music that could be featured in GTA 6 ahead of the game's release as part of its marketing push.
More billboards from Spotify IG https://t.co/yQE5NmmmsI pic.twitter.com/CLX6lK3MIW
— Tex2 (@TexFunz2) September 16, 2026 Some have also theorized that GTA 6 may have some kind of Spotify integration, allowing users to listen to their own Spotify playlists in-game. Given how much money Rockstar spends on curating music for its games and how much effort goes into crafting its radio stations, it seems difficult to imagine this, but it's entirely possible. Either way, it's clear Spotify has some kind of partnership with Rockstar Games on GTA 6.
Rockstar previously teamed up with Netflix to debut the first gameplay trailer for GTA 6, resulting in the premiere being the most-watched thing on the streamer during its first week. Rockstar Games personally pitched the idea to Netflix, so it wouldn't be surprising if a similar thing is happening with Spotify. Rockstar is also planning to do all kinds of unprecedented marketing in Miami, with signage being built as we speak in the city.
GTA 6 will officially be two months away from release this Saturday, so it wouldn't be surprising if Rockstar plans to put an end to all the teasing and unveil what it's doing with Spotify by the end of the week.

post_src_ign_68ba90b56d7d1844.title: Lanterns Midseason Trailer for Last 3 Episodes Leaves Fans Feeling Like They've Got 2 Seasons in 1
post_src_ign_68ba90b56d7d1844.description: HBO has released a midseason trailer for hit DC Universe show Lanterns, and it’s packed with tantalizing details on where the final three episodes will go.
post_src_ign_68ba90b56d7d1844.content:
HBO has released a midseason trailer for hit DC Universe show Lanterns, and it’s packed with tantalizing details on where the final three episodes will go.
Warning! Spoilers for Lanterns follow...
Early on, Lanterns set up the impending death of Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan, and based on this teaser, the show will see Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart try to solve the mystery of his murder. We see Sinestro here again, no doubt stewing the pot, as well as Nathan Fillion’s Guy Gardner. The show really has evolved into Lanterns, plural.
The blackest night is yet to come. Catch up on #Lanterns and stream new episodes Sundays on HBO Max. pic.twitter.com/1avM6N8Cdv
— HBO Max (@hbomax) September 17, 2026 There’s so much to talk about here. Stewart and Jordan have a catch-up after the dramatic events of last Sunday’s episode, which left both without the Green Lantern ring (Stewart by choice, Jordan because it was taken from him). It sounds like they will continue to be at each other’s throats during the rest of the season. Guy Gardner shows up to talk to Stewart, who is behind bars. “I can’t help you solve this murder,” Gardner tells Stewart. “It’s bad optics.” why is Stewart in jail in the first place?
We also see Sinestro saying “Hal didn’t have to die in vain… I know a way.” Is this some sort of resurrection plan? Something else? Whatever it is, I’m sure Sinestro’s plan is nefarious and very very yellow.
Through all this is the mystery of Noah Macon, born to lawyer Billy Macon and Sheridan County Sheriff's Department sheriff Kerry Kane. The last episode hinted that his conception may have been a "miracle" performed by the Manhunter. If so, does he have a bit of Manhunter in him? In the final three episodes, we’ll see him older and playing as a quarterback for his high school football team. I’m sure Noah’s fate will be tied to the end of the series in some way.
Whatever the case, fans are praising the trailer for making it feel like Lanterns is two seasons in one. The last episode really did feel like a season ender, and based on these final three episodes, we’re jumping forward significantly — and closer in time to last summer’s DCU kickstarter, Superman.
“I feel Hal isn't actually dead the way this trailer makes it out,” one fan on the Lanterns subreddit said. “I'm ready for the twists!!” “Don't die don't die don't die,” another pleaded. “This trailer focuses too much on his death. Any one else feel that? It's like they REALLY want us to believe he’s dead,” another pondered. “Or am I just coping?”
While we wait to find out, check out IGN’s review of Lanterns Episode 5.

post_src_ign_9d2ba00c46d920c6.title: BBC Wants Doctor Who Back in 2028/29, as Search Begins For New Production Team
post_src_ign_9d2ba00c46d920c6.description: Doctor Who fans will need to wait until at least 2028 or 2029 for the BBC's flagship sci-fi series to return.
post_src_ign_9d2ba00c46d920c6.content:
Doctor Who fans will need to wait until at least 2028 or 2029 for the BBC's flagship sci-fi series to return. 
That's according to official documentation set out by the BBC today, as it begins its process to find a fresh production team to take on the long-running series. 
As previously announced, the BBC is beginning a "tendering" process where it takes pitches from various production studios to pick up the franchise and produce new episodes. As of today, this process has now officially begun, with the BBC setting out its own expectations for the series' future and criteria that any production crew will need to meet. 
The headline here is the BBC's stated aim to air new episodes of Doctor Who in 2028/29 — a date that's still years away but still feels somewhat ambitious. There's also a sense of caution, as the tender would be for a single season of episodes, to only be extended to a second season "at BBC's discretion."
This situation follows the disastrous end to Doctor Who's most recent era, which collapsed after Disney chose not to renew its co-funding agreement, prompting star Ncuti Gatwa to leave in a reshot ending to the most recent season. Plans to wrap up the series' remaining narrative threads fell through, too, with an announced Christmas special from showrunner Russell T. Davies later confirmed to be scrapped.
Unsurprisingly, the BBC has stated that it wants to continue making Doctor Who as a multi-episode series (so no Doctor Who movies yet, then). There's also mention of the need to produce specials, which strongly suggests that the BBC wants to bring back the series' regular Christmas episode slot. (Hey, maybe Russell T. Davies will get invited back for that? Or, perhaps not.)
Digging a little deeper, the BBC has stated that it will only consider bids that meet at least two regional Ofcom critera. This refers to a list of considerations set out to ensure the BBC's output represents the whole of the U.K., grouped into three main categories: that the production has a substantive base inside the U.K. (but outside Greater London), and that 70% of production spend plus at least 50% of off-screen talent must fall under the same criteria. 
Specifically, the BBC states, it "has a preference for a Wales qualification," reflecting the production base and cultural home of the series for the past few decades. Finally, the deadline for production companies to submit their tender bids is on October 1 — not long away at all. 
All of that said, this first stage of the process requires only a three-page pitch document, with a brief editorial outline for the series and ideas for specials. Shortlisted bids will then be taken forward to the next stage of the process, which will last around six months in total. 
Guidelines set out by the BBC state that the series must include a companion character to "serve as an access point for audiences whilst also challenging, supporting, and influencing the Doctor." Existing villains can also be encorporated, though the BBC states that it is keen to "not be overly reliant on existing Doctor Who lore." No preference is stated for the format of the season's storytelling, however, which could form one long story arc or "monster of the week" standalone episodes.
A timetable put forth by the BBC notes that interviews with production companies will take place by the end of January 2027, with the BBC's decision to be made in March. While several production companies have expressed interest so far, it's believed that the frontrunner to win the tender will be the BBC's own commercial arm, BBC Studios. Certainly, the documentation laid out today suggests the process might be more complicated for a U.S. company to navigate.
If all runs smoothly and a production company is found by next March, this would leave slightly more than 18 months for the writing, casting and filming of new episodes in time for a 2028 airing (let alone the need for post-production). My money would be on a 2029 return, but time will tell. Last month, former Doctor Who writer and actor Mark Gatiss believed that, despite this process, the show would likely not return anytime soon, in order to let the franchise rest for a while longer.

post_src_ign_9d992e2f62e8120a.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Campaign Trailer Reveals Death Stranding Star Mads Mikkelsen
post_src_ign_9d992e2f62e8120a.description: Activision has revealed Casino Royale and Death Stranding star Mads Mikkelsen as a major antagonist in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
post_src_ign_9d992e2f62e8120a.content:
Activision has revealed Casino Royale and Death Stranding star Mads Mikkelsen as a major antagonist in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
Mikkelsen's involvement was revealed in a campaign trailer for Modern Warfare 4, which premiered during today's Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 broadcast. An official press release mentions that the game will focus on "the threat of a weapon that could overturn the world order in the hands of the villainous Archer." 
Sounds like Mikkelsen is Archer? Here he is in the campaign trailer:
"Price is on the run, conflict has erupted on the Korean Peninsula, and a catastrophic weapon of war is on the verge of falling into the wrong hands," reads a blurb for Modern Warfare 4's story. "Following the assassination of General Shepherd in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Task Force 141 has been disbanded when its leader, John Price, goes on the run. There’s a growing conflict between the remnants of 141, as Ghost questions Price's unlawful methods. Was Price right to take the law into his own hands, or has he betrayed everything he once stood for? Regardless, there’s a target on his back as Ghost and Gaz are tasked to capture or kill their former captain.
"In parallel with the Korean invasion and the ongoing manhunt for Price lies an even greater threat.  An unknown weapon of war is being delivered to a dangerous enemy known only as The Archer. What’s the weapon capable of, and what are the Archer’s motives in acquiring it?"
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches on October 23, with campaign early access live on October 16 for those who pre-order the Standard Digital Edition or Vault Edition of the game.
For more, catch up on everything announced during today's Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 broadcast right here.

post_src_ign_a31dd787779c29b0.title: GTA 6 Soundtrack Gets Physical CD and Vinyl Release, Rockstar Confirms
post_src_ign_a31dd787779c29b0.description: Rockstar will launch a physical edition of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack, a new leak has revealed.
post_src_ign_a31dd787779c29b0.content:
Rockstar will launch a $125 physical edition of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack, available on limited edition vinyl.
The news was broken this afternoon by the ever-reliable billbil-kun at Dealabs, while Rockstar announced the soundtrack itself a few minutes later. The collection of music will be published by Rockstar Games and Atlantic Records on November 19 — the same day as GTA 6 hits digital game stores. 
A double LP vinyl edition will be sold for $50, while a double CD version will sell for $20. For collectors, though, there's the limited edition vinyl set which contains "two transparent magenta discs filled with blue liquid," plus exclusive artwork. This is the one you'll pay $125 for. All editions are available for preorder now.
This news is somewhat ironic, considering the fact that GTA 6 itself will not get a physical launch on a disc, something that has sparked complaints from fans who want to own an actual copy of the upcoming blockbuster rather than an empty box.
Today's announcement follows a spate of teases by music streaming service Spotify both online and across billboards in New York, Los Angeles, and Miami. The teases continued online via the social media accounts of an array of artists, including Travis Scott and Keith Richards, that suggested they were also involved somehow with GTA 6. Now, we know why.
Travis Scott and Keith Richards are among the first batch of artists confirmed to have contributed music to the new album, with more tracks to be announced. Spotify will be one of the many places to stream the soundtrack online, meanwhile.
Indeed, Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album is now available for pre-save via major streaming services, where you can also listen to the first six tracks.

Bonus points if you like cats. post_src_ign_b16d37a2e0509b2d.content:
If you're a gamer who likes organizing your physical collection and you're looking for a new cozy game to play, indie developer ODIUS and publisher Loopr Partners's My Cat Scattered Games: Tidy Videogame Supermarket might be exactly what you want. Bonus points if you like cats. My Cat Scattered Games is a literal title: your in-game cat has taken your gargantuan physical games collection (represented here as funny, legally distinct versions of their real-life counterparts) and, as cats do, scattered them all over your the place. It's up to you to pick them all up and reorganize them on your shelves. 
You can organize over 6,000 games and consoles such as "Lovable Kombat," "Mega Bavario 64," and "Red Spirit 2" for systems like the "Kekstation 2" and "Y-box." You'll also need to rescue your cat, who after making this mess, somehow got itself trapped in a claw machine. Check out the first trailer above and the first screenshots in the gallery below.
"The job sounds simple enough," the developer says. "Pick up a game, identify its platform, find the right section, and put it back on the shelf. But with thousands of discs, cartridges, consoles, and other gaming treasures scattered across the store, keeping everything organized is easier said than done. Each shelf can hold up to three different games and ten copies of each title, giving players plenty of room to develop their own sorting strategy. As the store gradually comes back together, players can discover parody game covers, jokes, and references inspired by different eras of video game history."
You'll unlock ways to speed up your sorting and organization as you progress, but there are no ways to fail the game or lose. It's completely cozy and go-at-your-own-pace. [Editor's Note: It's almost like this was built for me and my mild OCD.] My Cat Scattered Games will be released for PC on October 9, and you can wishlist it on Steam if you're interested.

post_src_ign_c21f05d48bc53254.title: Valor Mortis Costs $40 Because of 'The Craziest Fall in the History of This Business'
post_src_ign_c21f05d48bc53254.description: Promising first-person action soulslike Valor Mortis has a confirmed $40 price point, which was settled upon by its publisher because of the fall crush fueled by GTA 6.
post_src_ign_c21f05d48bc53254.content:
Promising first-person action soulslike Valor Mortis has a confirmed $40 price point, which was settled upon by its publisher because of the fall crush fueled by GTA 6.
“We have had many discussions over the past year about the price of Valor Mortis,” publisher Lyrical Games said in a statement. “We believe the game has the quality, fidelity, and playtime in its 20-hour story to go toe-to-toe with many ‘full-price’ titles. Still, this Fall is stacked and there’s high demand for your time and money.”
Valor Mortis was already delayed from September 24 to October 13 to avoid the likes of Remedy’s Control Resonant and Konami’s Silent Hill: Townfall, but it also faces the looming launch of GTA 6 a month later. The hope is that by going with a cheaper price than some of its competitors it’ll stand out further, but what comes with that is the risk that some will feel it’s not as good.
In an interview with The Game Business, Lyrical Games boss Blake Rochkind expanded on the decision, admitting the price was something “we’ve really agonized over.”
“My biggest concern was that it would send the wrong message about the game. But this decision is made out of confidence,” he said.
“We find ourselves as one of the only new IPs launching in what is objectively the craziest fall in the history of this business. Not only do you have GTA looming large in November, now you have the Zelda remake, Control coming out in a couple of weeks, Silent Hill: Townfall, Phantom Blade Zero, Gears of War, Call of Duty... By virtue of the development schedule, the cards we’ve been dealt is that we are one of the only new IPs launching this fall.
“We are pretty confident in Valor Mortis. But ultimately, the worst thing we could do is not push our chips in and say, ‘We want this to be a game that you can pick up alongside these other great games.’”
This latter point is that Valor Mortis could be a game people buy as well as another, perhaps more expensive game, and a $40 price point makes that decision easier. Perhaps someone plans to buy GTA 6, which at its cheapest costs $80, but wouldn't mind snapping up Valor Mortis at half the price to play in the weeks beforehand.
Or maybe they will play Control Resonant and also Valor Mortis, or any other combination. “Going with this price point will help us be an ‘and’ game,” Rochkind said.
It’s worth noting that Valor Mortis is a day one Xbox Game Pass release, although Rochkind insisted this had nothing to do with the pricing decision.
From the creators of Ghostrunner, Valor Mortis is a first-person soulslike where you rise from death as a former soldier of Napoleon’s army, only to die over and over again battling shambling corpses and wild monsters. You can get a rundown on Valor Mortis in our recent preview.

post_src_ign_c477b55af420e84b.title: Moza Will Debut First PlayStation-Licensed Racing Wheels at Tokyo Game Show 2026
post_src_ign_c477b55af420e84b.description: The three new direct-drive products feature native support for Gran Turismo 7.
post_src_ign_c477b55af420e84b.content:
Moza has confirmed it will publicly showcase its upcoming range of officially licensed PlayStation racing products for the first time at Tokyo Game Show 2026. The new range on display will include the Moza R5S Pro Racing Simulator, the R16S Ultra Racing Simulator, and R16S Ultra Direct Drive wheel base.
The lineup includes an entry level package, a more powerful, high-performance package, and a standalone wheelbase for users who may already own a Moza rim (and are only seeking the PlayStation compatibility that needs to be baked into the wheel bases themselves in order to function on Sony consoles).
The debut will also mark the beginning of Moza’s collaboration with Gran Turismo 7 developer Polyphony Digital. From launch, Moza’s PlayStation racing lineup will support Gran Turismo 7 and “a growing selection of compatible racing titles,” according to the announcement.
The long-awaited PlayStation products are arriving after years of requests from racing sim enthusiasts for Moza to collaborate with Sony on a licensed racing wheel range.
While you wait for Moza’s new PlayStation products, get up to speed on what else is out there with our most recent shortlist of 10 racing wheel suggestions for PC, Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and even Nintendo Switch. Based on how much you have available to spend (and how serious you plan on taking your sim racing), it should give you a little more clarity on the strengths and weaknesses of all the wisest low-price, mid-range, and high-end options available today.
Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

post_src_ign_d49343fdf3edf32e.title: Hideo Kojima Announces It Star Bill Skarsgard Will Portray Physint's Main Character
post_src_ign_d49343fdf3edf32e.description: It star Bill Skarsgard will portray Physint's main character, Hideo Kojima has just confirmed.
post_src_ign_d49343fdf3edf32e.content:
It star Bill Skarsgård will portray Physint's main character, Hideo Kojima has just announced, days after the bombshell revelation that PlayStation had walked away from the project, which will now be published by Xbox instead.
Skarsgård will play Physint's unnamed lead character and protagonist, and joins the previously announced trio of actors on the project: Charlee Fraser, Don Lee and Minami Hamabe. While still years from release, Kojima said today that Physint was continuing to making "steady progress." 
Behind the scenes footage of Physint's early production premiered during today's Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 broadcast. A poster for the game has also revealed its tagline: "The Next Cold War Begins."
"I'm delighted to confirm the lead role for Physint will be Bill Skarsgård,” Kojima said today. "We are both long-time fans of each other's work, and we've decided to embark on this new adventure together. The costume fittings, scans, and camera tests we conducted with Bill and Charlee earlier this year gave me tremendous confidence in the direction of the project. My vision of the final form became much more solidified."
Skarsgård is best known for playing creepy clown Pennywise in It, It: Chapter Two, and It: Welcome to Derry. He's also appeared in Nosferatu, Barbarian, The Crow, and John Wick: Chapter 4, as well as TV series such as Castle Rock and Hemlock Grove.
"Physint is the culmination of more than 40 years of my career," Kojima added, "a project that will redefine 'action-espionage', unbound by any existing genres in digital entertainment. The project conitnues to make steady progress. We're also making progress on casting, talent scans, and collaborations with outside creators. There are still many exciting cast announcements to come in future, so please stay tuned for further updates.
"Finally, I would liek to sincerely thank all of our players, fans, and community members for tuning in and for your continued support. I would also like to thank our partners at Xbox for believing in our vision and walking this parth toward the future alongside us. We are incredibly excited about the road ahead and look forward to sharing much more with you in the future. Please stay tuned!"
Last week, it was reported that Sony ditched Kojima due to budget concerns and missed deadlines on Physint, which is in development to arrive after the Metal Gear Solid creator's other upcoming project, OD. Analysts speculated that lower sales of Death Stranding's sequel may also have played a part in spooking PlayStation, though others suggested that publishing Kojima games has always been about more than just raw sales figures.
For more, catch up on everything announced during today's Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 broadcast right here.

post_src_ign_e7b5614b52e98fb4.title: GTA 5 Franklin Voice Actor Clears the Air After Calling Out Twitch Star Kai Cenat for Allegedly Breaking Promise to a Young Fan
post_src_ign_e7b5614b52e98fb4.description: The voice actor behind GTA 5’s Franklin went viral after revealing his personal disagreement with famous Twitch steamer Kai Cenat, but the two stars are on good terms again.
post_src_ign_e7b5614b52e98fb4.content:
The voice actor behind GTA 5’s Franklin went viral after revealing his personal disagreement with famous Twitch steamer Kai Cenat, but the two stars are on good terms again.
Shawn ‘Solo’ Fonteno is the voice behind one of Grand Theft Auto’s most iconic characters, Franklin Clinton. He made an appearance on Kai Cenat’s Twitch stream as a special guest back in 2024, where he took the influencer on a tour of the neighborhoods in Los Angeles that appeared in the game’s fictional city of Los Santos.
However, Solo said this was likely the last stream he’d ever do with Cenat due to the broadcaster’s interaction with a young fan that happened during their outing.
In a September 2026 episode of the Dope As Usual podcast, Solo explained that Kai Cenat approached a young fan during the stream who came from a struggling family.  According to Solo, Cenat had offered to buy the fan a motorcycle — but Solo says he never made good on that promise.
“This was a family that didn’t have much at all, bro,” he recalled. “It was probably 15 people living in a one-bedroom home. I know these people, and I help them out at times. …Kai was cool, cordial with them, talking to them, ‘What you want? What can I get you?’ And the kid was like, ‘I wanna bike, can you get me a bike?’ He said, ‘What kind of bike?’ and the kid said, ‘A motorcycle!’ He said, ‘We gon’ make it happen.’
“I persisted to keep calling after that… let about a week go by, and texted, texted, tried to call, ‘Hey man, honor that [promise] with this kid, bro. It’s just a bike. [It’d] probably be about a thousand dollars, twelve hundred dollars or less, I don’t know, but you gave that kid this promise. And now you’re making me look bad, because I brought you here, and you gave this kid that promise.’”
Solo said he even approached Kai’s friend and fellow streamer Fanum about the issue, who the actor says ignored him. 
“I’m standing on it, man,” he continued. “I’ll look into any one of these cameras like, ‘Bro, you a f**ked up dude for that.’ To me. You’re a very f**ked up dude. I don’t give a f**k how you feel about it. To me, that was not cool. If I make a promise, especially to a kid, I’mma honor it.”
The podcast went viral, prompting a wave of backlash toward Kai Cenat for allegedly failing to keep his promise to the child. Fans were convinced that he and Solo now had bad blood as a result of this issue — but just a day later, Solo confirmed that he and Kai were on good terms once more.
Solo revealed the news in an Instagram comment on September 16, which he wrote in response to a clip from the podcast episode. “I just talked to Kai and it was an honest mistake and it’s fixed. Thanks @kaicenat,” he said.
GTA fervor is at an all-time high after Rockstar’s immensely-popular preview for Grand Theft Auto 6 aired on Netflix last month. Fans can’t wait for the highly-anticipated game to finally release in November, and with major music artists and platforms like Spotify dropping cheeky hints on social media and billboards across Los Angeles, it’s clear there’s a lot more in store as the clock ticks down to launch in two months.

post_src_ign_f9d01ee1fd2577fd.title: Explosive Elon Musk Documentary Likely to Be Dropped by Universal, Report Claims
post_src_ign_f9d01ee1fd2577fd.description: Universal is reportedly reconsidering its release of a revealing Elon Musk documentary, despite it receiving rave reviews at recent film festivals.
post_src_ign_f9d01ee1fd2577fd.content:
Universal is reportedly reconsidering its release of a revealing Elon Musk documentary, despite it receiving rave reviews at recent film festivals.
Weighing in at four hours (with a 10-minute intermission), Musk is the work of prolific filmmaker Alex Gibney, who secured access to various figures close to the Grok owner in his personal life, as well as those who comment on his political influence.
But while an informative documentary on the world's richest man would likely put bums on seats, The Hollywood Reporter claims that Universal is now likely to drop the movie's full release.
Universal paid millions for the rights to release Musk back in 2023, before the now-trillionaire fully aligned himself with President Donald Trump. Today, however, there's reportedly hesitancy over launching the film, with the expected outcome now that the movie rights will be returned to Gibney for him to sell again elsewhere.
In a thread on Twitter/X, which Musk owns, former Wall Street Journal and NBC News journalist Matt Rivera recounted watching the documentary at Venice Film Festival, where it received a five-minute ovation, and listed an array of eye-opening details regarding the film's contents.
These includes purported claims by Musk's former partner Ashley St. Clair that the trillionaire knew the 2024 election result hours before it was made official due to "lasers in space." The movie also includes Musk's reaction to the Wall Street Journal's reporting of his alleged drug use, and discussion of the NDA that St. Clair claims she was asked to sign after giving birth to one of Musk's 14 known children.
The "lasers in space" claim previously caught the eye of Musk's attorney Alex Spiro, who appeared to debunk the phrase having any other meaning than a reference to how Starlink satellites communicate in space. In a letter to Gibney and the film's producers at Jigsaw Productions, reported by NPR, Spiro stated that the filmmaker had been put "on notice." 
"Starlink was not connected to vote tabulation," Spiro wrote. "Election officials in multiple states, independent cybersecurity researchers, and fact-checkers publicly refuted the Starlink vote-rigging claim in November 2024, and nothing since has revived it. Starlink's satellites communicate by laser inter-satellite link; that is what 'lasers in space' describes. You are therefore on notice, before release, that the insinuation is false, that the material refuting it is public, and that you chose not to be told the rest."
In response, Jigsaw stated that it had a "right to engage in open debate and fact-based examinations of powerful public figures" protected by the First Amendment, "something that should be recognized and defended by all Americans, including the associates of Elon Musk, who has proclaimed himself to be a 'free speech absolutist.'"
Other former partners and family members of Musk also feature in the documentary, though Musk (perhaps unsurprisingly) declined to take part. Instead, re-enactments of his public comments are made by a CGI replacement as a "literal staging of the film's theme," Rivera wrote, "a man who manufactures his reality."
Musk has recently fired off a string of social media posts regarding the movie, dubbing it as a "hit piece that misses" and "a false film" that was also "boring." Neither Musk or Spiro have seen the film, and the two sides have clashed over Gibney's refusal to discuss its material with them, while Gibney has stated that Musk refused to take part and be interviewed.
"This isn't the hit job Musk claims," Rivera concluded, after watching the movie. "At times, it bends over backward to be fair. But it pierces Musk's mythos, playing some stories twice to expose contradictions and posing open questions: What's with all the kids? What is he doing with all that data?"
Universal ditching Musk would not be the only recent example of a distributor dropping a documentary that could make for uncomfortable viewing. Amazon previously walked away from the Sam Altman documentary Artificial, days after signing a $50 billion deal with Altman's company OpenAI. Musk was also featured in that film, which will now see its release via indie distributor Neon.
The Hollywood Reporter also highlights the current situation with Musk's streaming release, which HBO has paid for (and also contributed further funds to the film's budget when needed during filming). HBO will likely soon be owned by Warner Bros., in a deal backed by CEO David Ellison and his billionaire father Larry. Musk reportedly features Larry Ellison in an unfavorable light — so it will be interesting to see if the documentary's streaming launch goes ahead as planned, too.
Image credit: Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images.

post_src_nasa_news_1b65852549489970.title: Passion Meets Precision at NASA’s Flight Research Lab
post_src_nasa_news_1b65852549489970.description: Long before they helped shape NASA’s future aerospace breakthroughs, Derek Abramson, Justin Hall, and Justin Link were in their garages and homes building radio‑controlled aircraft, testing new ideas, and flying their creations at hobby events. That early passion now fuels the work of NASA’s Dale Reed Subscale Flight Research Laboratory at the agency’s Armstrong Flight […]
post_src_nasa_news_1b65852549489970.content:
4 min read
Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater)
Derek Abramson, Dale Reed Subscale Flight Research Laboratory chief engineer, left, communicates with the Edwards Air Force Base air traffic control tower for approval to fly the Alta-X drone near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. Justin Link, small uncrewed aircraft pilot, second from left, and laboratory chief pilot Justin Hall await flight clearance. Researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston developed the advanced guidance and navigation system known as the Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution (SPLICE) experiment, which is installed on the Alta-X. SPLICE will help spacecraft land precisely and detect and avoid potential hazards, which is critical for NASA missions to the Moon and to Mars.NASA/Ryan Kline
Long before they helped shape NASA’s future aerospace breakthroughs, Derek Abramson, Justin Hall, and Justin Link were in their garages and homes building radio‑controlled aircraft, testing new ideas, and flying their creations at hobby events. That early passion now fuels the work of NASA’s Dale Reed Subscale Flight Research Laboratory at the agency’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.
At NASA Armstrong’s subscale flight lab, the team turns that lifelong enthusiasm into mission-focused innovation. The laboratory supports research that ranges from advanced navigation systems for future landings on the Moon and Mars to emerging aeronautics concepts that need quick, low-cost evaluation. NASA’s small, remotely piloted and autonomous aircraft allow engineers to explore ideas that could be difficult, risky or expensive to test at full scale.
Skilled team
Abramson, Hall, and Link play key roles in that work. Abramson serves as the laboratory’s chief engineer. Hall is the chief pilot. Link is a drone pilot. Together, they integrate emerging aerospace technologies with the lab’s subscale aircraft fleet and, when needed, design and build aircraft or flight experiments to evaluate new concepts.
Derek Abramson, chief engineer at the Dale Reed Subscale Flight Research Laboratory at NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, is shown with his Kalt Cyclone radio-controlled helicopter in the mid-1980s. Abramson loved flying this aircraft as a child, and he has been an aviation enthusiast for as long as he can remember.Derek Abramson
Abramson’s expertise, built through service in the U.S. Navy and the aerospace industry, centers on technical oversight, management, and system design. Hall is known for creative approaches to problem solving and uses practical methods to address technical challenges and maintain flight safety. Link specializes in designing and fabricating research vehicles and draws on extensive hands-on experience to understand what works, and what does not, in flight. 
On weekends, the team often tinkers in their garages or hangars building radio-control aircraft, researching hobby trends, or exploring new technologies. You might see them flying their creations at hobby events or attending trade shows. Their passion for flight brought Abramson, Hall, and Link together years before they one-by-one joined NASA more than a decade ago, though each discovered that spark in a different way.
Early influences
Abramson’s interest began as a child with rubber-band powered stick and tissue aircraft and radio-controlled models. His early aviation pursuits led to his first solo flight while in high school and a pilot’s license. In the Navy, he worked on multiple aircraft, including EA-6B and the F-18, as an avionics technician. As an engineer, he supported the B-1 and CV-22 Osprey aircraft flight tests. As an intern at NASA Armstrong, he used his operational and engineering experience on remotely piloted and autonomous aircraft.
Hall’s interest grew after seeing historic aircraft including the Mach 3 SR-71 fly over his elementary school playground and watching Space Shuttle Challenger land from above his dad’s shoulders. He has built and flown model and remotely piloted aircraft for as long as he can remember. His reputation flying radio-controlled hobby aircraft at fly-ins and trade events led to an offer to fly subscale aircraft at NASA.
Justin Hall, chief pilot at the Dale Reed Subscale Flight Research Laboratory at NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, stands in front of a radio-controlled aircraft with his dad, David Hall, in August 2020. David Hall built the Gee Bee aircraft years earlier but was unable to fly it due to his health. He asked his son to fly the aircraft so he could see it in the air, which Justin did the day of this photo. Shortly afterward, David Hall passed away.Justin Hall
Justin link, drone pilot at the Dale Reed Subscale Flight Research Laboratory at NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California, and his dad, Don Link, hold a Firebird radio-controlled aircraft on the day of its first flight in September 2023. It was a project they worked on together. Don Link reduced the dimensions of the original larger-scale model aircraft and drew the plans, while Justin Link manufactured composite molds and built the aircraft from scratch.Justin Link
Link was five years old when he built balsa-wood aircraft with his dad and flew them in a field near their home. As he grew older, his hobby expanded to include radio-controlled cars, boats, helicopters, and aircraft. Aviation runs deep in Link’s family. His great grandfather served in the U.S. Army Air Corps, his grandfathers served in the U.S. Air Force, and his dad was an Air Force avionics technician. Link raced sailplanes, competed with scaled warbird aircraft, and was encouraged by family and friends to pursue an aviation profession. He has worked with large drones for more than 11 years, focusing on research and development, composite materials, and specialized fabrication methods.
Together, the team applies its experience and knowledge in rapid design, fabrication, integration and flight testing to bring new ideas to flight. Their work continues to support NASA’s missions across aeronautics, science, and exploration.

post_src_nasa_news_619140dcace834bc.title: NASA Visits Schools Strengthening Florida’s Skilled Workforce
post_src_nasa_news_619140dcace834bc.description: NASA recently awarded $10.5 million to seven organizations nationwide through its new State Hubs initiative. Elaine Ho, associate […]
post_src_nasa_news_619140dcace834bc.content:
NASA recently awarded $10.5 million to seven organizations nationwide through its new State Hubs initiative. Space Florida was selected for Project ORBIT, which aims to expand opportunities for middle and high school students, boost enrollment in key career and technical programs, and create a statewide portal connecting skilled workers with aerospace employers.
Elaine Ho, right, associate administrator for NASA’s Office of STEM Engagement, discusses training software with a student at Lyman High School in Longwood, Florida on on Aug. 27, 2026.Credit: NASA/Clayton Rougelot
Elaine Ho, associate administrator for NASA’s Office of STEM Engagement, joined local leaders and industry partners recently to see Space Florida Academy students in action at three Central Florida schools. Students at Lyman High School in Longwood, Florida, demonstrated their skills in aerospace engineering, robotics, building trades, welding, and more. Later, in Merritt Island, Florida, Ho and the other leaders stopped by the Aeronautics & Flight Exploration (AFEX) program and cloud computing classrooms at Merritt Island High School and the robotics lab at nearby Edgewood Junior/Senior High School.
Since its launch in August 2024, the Space Florida Academy has expanded from 23 to 42 participating school districts, preparing students for careers in aviation and aerospace, advanced manufacturing, construction, cybersecurity, logistics, and semiconductors.
Elaine Ho, center, poses for a photo with Space Florida representatives, public school officials, aerospace industry partners, and students at Edgewood Junior/Senior High School in Merritt Island, Florida on Aug. 27, 2026.Credit: NASA/Clayton Rougelot
“It’s all about showing students what’s possible and then giving them the tools to achieve it,” said Dean Cuke, Merritt Island High School AFEX astronautics and aviation flight instructor. “There are far more possible pathways to be part of the space industry than I think they realize. We’re showing them ways that they can attain that, through learning, through motivation and chasing after their dreams. I’m excited for them.”
Merritt Island High School juniors and student pilots Olivia Street and Troy Wallenburg have both benefited from the program.
“It makes you feel like you’re a part of something way bigger than just a high school class. I learned what I want to do when I grow up – to be a pilot,” Street said.
“My entire life, I’ve just loved space,” Wallenburg said. “It’s great knowing that I’m actually somewhat involved in it, too.”
A student in the Merritt Island High School Aeronautics and Flight Exploration program shows Elaine Ho, left, how to use a flight simulator on Aug. 27, 2026.Credit: NASA/Clayton Rougelot
“I’m so impressed by how this region holds so many opportunities for our students, who are incredibly capable of solving hard problems, who can build our hardware, who want to be part of something bigger than themselves,” Ho said. “NASA is really focused on ensuring that those opportunities are easier to reach.”

post_src_nasa_news_a5d6af81acb29740.description: NASA celebrated the full restoration of its Guam Remote Station with a ribbon-cutting on Sept. 10, closing out more than three years of recovery after Super Typhoon Mawar devastated the site in 2023. Engineers from across the agency completed the final and most complex step of the rebuild on July 1, when they returned the […]
post_src_nasa_news_a5d6af81acb29740.content:
On Sept. 10, 2026, NASA commemorated the completed repairs of the Guam Remote Station’s central antenna with a ribbon-cutting ceremony.Members of NASA, the Governor’s Office of Guam, military personnel, and family members gathered to celebrate the Guam Remote Station’s return to operations.NASA									
									The ribbon-cutting event was held in front of the repaired central antenna. As of 2026, the newly hardened station has withstood two super typhoons more powerful than Mawar with minimal damage.SCaN Deputy Manager for Network Operations Jena Garrahy addresses members of the Guam Remote Station ribbon-cutting event.NASA									
									Guam Remote Station Site Manager Kristopher Copple was among those recognized during the ceremony.Jena Garrahy (right), SCaN Deputy Manager for Network Operations, presents a certificate of recognition to Guam Remote Station Site Manager Kristopher Copple (left).NASA									
									NASA’s Guam Remote Station is key to the Tracking and Data Relay Satellite (TDRS) constellation maintaining continuous communications with the International Space Station.An artist’s concept of the International Space Station using NASA’s Tracking and Data Relay Satellite (TDRS) fleet to transmit data to Earth. NASA									
									A 2023 aerial photo of the Guam Remote Station prior to Super Typhoon Mawar landing on the island. Satellite image of NASA remote ground terminal located in Dededo area, Guam, released by U.S. commercial satellite company MAXAR.MAXAR									
									An aerial photo of the Guam Remote Station immediately after Super Typhoon Mawar struck the station.  of the station’s three ground antennas were demolished.Satellite image of NASA remote ground terminal located in Dededo area, Guam, released by U.S. commercial satellite company MAXAR. MAXAR									
NASA celebrated the full restoration of its Guam Remote Station with a ribbon-cutting on Sept. 10, closing out more than three years of recovery after Super Typhoon Mawar devastated the site in 2023. Engineers from across the agency completed the final and most complex step of the rebuild on July 1, when they returned the station’s central antenna to service.
A rainbow arcs over the newly repaired Guam Remote Station antennas.NASA
For nearly three decades, the Guam Remote Station has been one of three ground stations supporting NASA’s Tracking and Data Relay Satellites, or TDRS, a critical part of the Near Space Network. From 22,000 miles above Earth, the relays link spacecraft in low Earth orbit with the ground, allowing flight controllers to communicate with astronauts, command spacecraft, and receive mission data. The Guam station alone closes the “Zone of Exclusion,” a stretch of orbit beyond the relays’ line of sight. Without it, the International Space Station can lose contact with Earth for up to 20 minutes of every 90-minute orbit, an unacceptable risk for crewed missions.
On May 24, 2023, the Category 4 super typhoon struck Guam with 185 mph winds and more than 28 inches of rain, destroying two 16.5-meter antennas and damaging an 11-meter north antenna and the Inter Facility Link building at NASA’s station. The Zone of Exclusion reopened for the first time since 1998, cutting TDRS coverage to about 85% of a spacecraft’s orbit.
NASA made emergency repairs to the least-damaged antenna and borrowed two mobile terminals from the U.S. Army to expand coverage. The patchwork restored partial service within months, in time for a November 2023 spacewalk.
In early 2025, Congress dedicated disaster-relief funding to rebuild the ground station and harden the network against future storms. Construction began that summer and finished in summer 2026, when the rebuilt central antenna rejoined TDRS operations and the Zone of Exclusion closed once more. The same appropriation funded critical upgrades at three additional Near Space Network ground stations.
					The return to service of the Guam Remote Station’s central antenna represents far more than the restoration of a critical piece of infrastructure — it is a testament to the dedication, resilience, and ingenuity of the people who made it possible.
						Jena Garrahy
						SCaN Deputy Program Manager for Network Operations
At the ribbon-cutting, representatives from NASA’s SCaN (Space Communications and Navigation) Division joined the station’s workforce and local leaders to mark the central antenna’s return to service. The Guam team, which led debris removal, site security, and on-island recovery, was recognized for its  work to keep NASA connected to its missions through the outage and rebuild. A companion ceremony at NASA’s White Sands Complex in Las Cruces, New Mexico, honored the engineers and specialists across SCaN who supported the recovery off island.
“The return to service of the Guam Remote Station’s central antenna represents far more than the restoration of a critical piece of infrastructure — it is a testament to the dedication, resilience, and ingenuity of the people who made it possible,” said Jena Garrahy, Deputy Program Manager for Network Operations. “Through long days, challenging conditions, and unexpected obstacles, this team remained focused on the missions that depend on these critical assets every day.”
The Near Space Network is funded by SCaN, a division of NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate, at the agency’s Headquarters in Washington. The network is operated out of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland. Repairs of the Guam Remote Station were managed out of NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland.

post_src_nasa_news_aa372224af74f61b.description: Seasonal changes redistribute enough water around Earth to shift the planet’s center of mass back and forth by fractions of an inch relative to its geometric center. NASA scientists are on the case, tracking the oscillations because Earth’s center of mass is a crucial reference point for satellite navigation and elevation measurements. A team, led […]
post_src_nasa_news_aa372224af74f61b.content:
5 min read
Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater)
Water sloshing between the land and oceans shifts Earth’s center of mass relative to its geometric center. NASA scientists have developed a new technique using ultraprecise satellite tracking to estimate the displacement to within fractions of inches.NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio
Seasonal changes redistribute enough water around Earth to shift the planet’s center of mass back and forth by fractions of an inch relative to its geometric center. NASA scientists are on the case, tracking the oscillations because Earth’s center of mass is a crucial reference point for satellite navigation and elevation measurements.
A team, led by NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, has proposed a way to calculate the seasonal swings with extreme precision. The technique and findings are detailed in a new study published in Geophysical Journal International. The authors paint a vivid picture of springtime thaws, churning oceans, and dense winter air shifting massive surface loads from season to season.
The study isn’t the first attempt to pin down Earth’s center of mass. Scientists over the decades have pioneered several space-based techniques to define and locate it. But it’s a moving goalpost. If Earth were a hard blue marble, its center of mass would simply overlap its geometric center. In reality, the planet is sloshing and sagging under the weight of water, ice, and air. Because of this, Earth’s center of mass continually swivels around its geometric center by as much as several millimeters.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that
					supports HTML5 video
NASA’s Space Geodesy Project currently uses a variety of space- and land-based techniques to track Earth’s center of mass (also called the geocenter) moving up and down and side to side. This animation traces the millimeter-scale motion from 1993 to 2017.NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio
How accurate are existing methods to measure the size of the swivel? The last two international estimates, made in 2017 and 2023, differ by 0.27 inches (7 millimeters), about the height of three stacked nickels. The difference is almost as large as the motion itself.
To reduce uncertainty, JPL geoscientist Donald Argus led the development of a new technique based on ultraprecise satellite tracking.
Driven by gravity, satellites naturally orbit Earth’s center of mass, as if bound by invisible tethers. Tiny changes in the distance between satellites and ground stations reflect Earth’s shifting center of mass.
Using satellites to locate Earth’s center of mass is not a new idea. In fact, dense metal satellites, launched in 1976 and 1992, are dedicated exclusively to this purpose. Resembling 900-pound (408-kilogram) disco balls, both Laser Geodynamics Satellites (LAGEOS 1 and 2) are studded with reflective prisms and tracked with laser precision via ground stations globally distributed across more than 20 countries.
However, one limitation of satellite laser ranging is the uneven distribution of ground stations around Earth. The new technique improves accuracy in two ways: It adds GPS tracking into the mix along with orbital data from several satellites in low Earth orbit to provide a diverse array of targets. And it considers how the weight of water and ice deforms Earth’s crust, taking ground stations along for the ride.
The technique was developed by Argus along with researchers from JPL’s satellite orbit determination team, the University of Nevada, University of Montana, and the Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences in Germany.
“We’re now estimating the size of the movement of Earth’s mass center back and forth each year to be about half of what we believed it to be eight years ago,” said Argus. “Our findings suggest that the mass of Earth’s water and air moving between the hemisphere is smaller than previously thought.”
Felix Landerer, one of the study’s coauthors at JPL, noted that “while these movements might appear tiny, our modern world relies on extremely accurate positioning measurements. By unraveling and understanding the mechanisms that change reference systems, we can build better reference systems that ultimately benefit mapping and navigation — from global shipping logistics to precision agriculture.”
What they found
The study authors tracked Earth’s center of mass oscillating seasonally and attributed the cause to three categories: oceans, atmosphere, and continental water (made up of land ice, snow, lake and river water, soil moisture, and groundwater).
They found that snow accumulation in North America and Eurasia reaches a maximum in March and shifts Earth’s center of mass about 3 millimeters toward the North Pole. A month later, in April, rainwater in the Amazon River basin peaks at 2,400 gigatons, swinging Earth’s center of mass 2.2 millimeters toward South America. Monsoon water in southeast Asia attains a maximum of 600 gigatons six months later in November, adding slightly to the annual oscillation.
Between August and October, the oceans swell with meltwater and rain, and Earth’s center of mass shifts toward the South Pacific Ocean. The Pacific Ocean is so large that mass changes there overshadow the loss or gain in other oceans, though seasonal dynamics in the Mediterranean, Red, North, Baltic, and Barents seas all help shift Earth’s center of mass in their own small way.
The researchers used a model developed by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts to estimate how atmospheric changes affect Earth’s center of mass throughout the seasons. They found that cold, dense, winter air helps tip the scales over Arabia, Asia, and northern Africa around Dec. 21 each year, and over South America and South Africa around June 21.
The mass calculations in the study are consistent with observations made by the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment Follow-On (GRACE-FO) mission. Launched in 2018, the mission is made up of twin satellites that map monthly fluctuations in Earth’s gravitational pull due primarily to the mass movement of water above and below ground. The two satellites fly in precise formation, and when the lead satellite passes over a dense body, like a swollen river basin, the extra gravitational tug changes the distance between its twin by a small but measurable amount.
The GRACE-FO mission is a joint partnership between NASA and the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ). The next-generation GRACE-Continuity (GRACE-C) mission is targeting a launch in late 2028 to extend the nearly 25-year GRACE-series data record.

						Curiosity Postcard Celebrates Rover’s 5,000th Day on Mars
							JPEG (459.76 KB)
Description
While parked at a sand ridge nicknamed “Chocolatal,” NASA’s Curiosity Mars rover used its black-and-white navigation cameras to capture panoramas at two times of day. The first was taken on Aug. 30, 2026, at 9:56 a.m. local Mars time; the second was taken on Sep. 2, 2026, at 5:39 p.m. local Mars time. Those dates correspond to the 5,000th and 5,003rd Martian days, or sols, of the mission.
After being sent back to Earth, the two images were merged together. Color was added for an artistic interpretation of the scene, with blue representing the morning panorama and yellow representing the afternoon one. The resulting “postcard” is similar to past examples created with rover images, such as one taken in November 2021.
The rover’s deck can be seen in the foreground, including its can-shaped UHF antenna, used for sending data to orbiting spacecraft, and its finned Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (MMRTG), a nuclear power source, at its rear. The rover’s tracks can be seen trailing off in the distance. 
Curiosity is in the lower foothills of Mount Sharp, a 3-mile-tall (5-kilometer-tall) mountain that sits within Gale Crater. This image looks down toward the crater floor, with the crater rim barely perceptible on the horizon.
Curiosity was built by NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, which is managed by Caltech in Pasadena, California. JPL leads the mission on behalf of NASA’s Science Mission Directorate in Washington as part of NASA’s Mars Exploration Program portfolio.
To learn more about Curiosity, visit:
